residents.basis: HOUSED HERE BY THE DEAL, NOT RECORDED HERE (L354). The sources stop short of 1 July 1835 for this household and nothing puts it anywhere else; the town's rule (T-1386) counts it present, and no source says where it slept. The roof is the invention and the people are not.

persons.name: W Brannen
persons.note: THE ST CYR REGISTER OF 1833-1835 NAMES THIS PERSON IN THE PARISH. Read from church_1833_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G2c), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. church_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 31 July 1834 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1).

residents.research_note: MINTED FROM THE CONSOLIDATED CIVIC, CHURCH, PRESS, BOOK AND CENSUS EVIDENCE (T-0513, T-0514). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here is written unattested in its own block, because the lists that name this person name a person and not a family. What is claimed is that the sources cited on the member below name them at Chicago, and the grade is the owner's ratified ladder applied by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py --build and spent by tools/mint_civic_residents.py, which prints every refusal. docs/LIBERTIES.md L215 carries the liberty and the tension with L213.

persons.name: She Kauk
persons.note: CARDED FROM THE BORDERLINE ROSTER'S R6 (T-1376, stage `underdocumented`). Enrolled at Chicago in 1832 in the company the Black Hawk War roll heads INDIAN, with no 1835 corroboration and no card. The licence is R3's — the same roll, the same year, the same page — and the twenty men of Kercheval's company the town already carries were re-admitted under it. The roll prints him as `SHE KAUK`, company `INDIAN`, enrolled at `CHICAGO`. The research READ this name and WITHHELD it, and that refusal is not overturned: this record is a reconstruction of what the town looks like if the name is admitted at the limit of its own evidence, and it says so on its face. The reading, the source and the refusal stand at `civic:data/research/civic/records/blackhawk_war_1832_chicago.json#records/blackhawk_1832_098#0` in data/reconstruction/1835_borderline_roster.json. REVIEW REQUIRED: this card is a record of a Native person at Chicago in the three years of the removal, and AGENTS.md's standing constraint holds it for review by Native scholars or community organisations before any scene carrying it may be marked released. No figure is drawn (L1).
